newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bonds strengthen on stock market fall.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bonds strengthen on stock market fall.

text.p: Swedish bond yields were lower around midday on Monday as they benefited from a stock market fall and the crown softened to mark on a weaker dollar.
Dealers expected the yield curve to steepen as investors would transfer money from the bourse to T-bills and bonds with short maturities.
"The stock market fall may have a slight positive affect on interest rates as investors have to invest their money somewhere," said Peter Lindquist, analyst with HSBC Midland.
"They are mainly changing into short maturities, T-bills, as they don't want to take any interest rate risk."
The six-month T-bill rate fell three basis points to 4.34 percent and the 10-year bond yield fell two to 6.62 percent.
The crown softened to 4.3770 against the mark from 4.3650 late on Friday, hurt by a softer dollar, and dealers saw it weakening further.
"People are talking about a target of 1.8050 marks against the dollar and it is then natural for mark/crown to come up," one dealer said.
The crown was expected to trade between 4.37 and 4.40 against the mark, dealers said.
